title: A “One Species, Two Standards” Bidirectional Regulation Protocol Based on Ecological Niche Property Encoding
content: The production side of Chinese medicine has long run two parallel systems of objectives: medicinal-material production aims to make medicinal properties pronounced, whereas food-material production aims to keep the directional predilection balanced. The two, however, have lacked a unified formal objective function and a testable research design. Drawing on the ecological niche property (ENP) framework—distinct from the suitable-area modeling of the ecological niche model (ENM); in this paper “niche” denotes a habitat coding niche—this study defines habitat parameters as the coding variables of medicinal properties and the whole medicinal-property vector, which connects directly to formulation rules, as the output variable. It proposes a “sender-free encoding” model of rule-governed mapping and, on that basis, designs a symmetric, parallel bidirectional regulation experiment on the same species: a medicinal line that strengthens the predilection and a food line that attenuates it. The primary endpoint is the medicinal-property vector measured by a two-layer measurement instrument (Instrument A: multi-source literature agreement; Instrument B: a blinded expert panel). Three hypothesis lines, E1–E3, are set for reliability, construct validity, and between-group effect size, with falsification conditions and sample-size re-estimation rules specified in advance. The paper is organized by evidence status. Part I reports the completed calibration of Instrument A: 10 species and 6 sources, with the four mainstream sources showing perfect agreement (1.000) across three dimensions. After the extended sources were included, four-nature κ = 0.913 and Gwet AC1 = 0.927; for meridian tropism, pairwise set agreement was 0.813, species-level complete agreement 0.600, and subset agreement 1.000, with all meridian disagreements being strict subset additions; E1 received exploratory support. A sensitivity analysis treating “not recorded” as a valid category yielded κ = 0.424, indicating that the complete-case framing is optimistic. Part II presents the preregistered content for E2 and E3: the primary effect size is fixed as Cliff’s δ (δ ≥ 0.33), the pilot includes no fewer than 12 units per line, and the confirmatory sample size is approximately 64 units per group. This protocol does not promise clinical efficacy; it tests only the measurability and regulability of the medicinal-property construct.
